enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Let him speak on his own: Home Assistant automations, the API and `winston announce` send him something to say.

chime.title: Chime
chime.description: Sound played before an announcement, so it is clearly a notification. Empty for none.

quiet_hours.title: Quiet hours
quiet_hours.description: HH:MM-HH:MM when announcements are not spoken, only sent to Discord. Empty for never quiet.

discord.title: Also to Discord
discord.description: always: every announcement; fallback: when nothing can speak it (quiet hours, no speaker connected); never.

ha_event.title: Home Assistant event
ha_event.description: Event type an automation fires with data {text, context} to announce.

context.title: Context
context.description: Details he keeps for follow-up questions but does not read out.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Hand hard questions to Claude. Uses the Claude Code login on this machine, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (claude setup-token) or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Only the question leaves the house.

model.title: Model
model.description: Claude model the question goes to. Opus is best at hard questions, Sonnet and Haiku are faster and cheaper.

effort.title: Effort
effort.description: Reasoning effort. Low answered in about 3 to 5 s; each step up is slower.

max_usd_per_day.title: Budget per day (USD)
max_usd_per_day.description: Past it the tool refuses until midnight. A Max 5x plan's monthly Agent SDK credit is 100 USD.

max_usd_per_question.title: Budget per question (USD)
max_usd_per_question.description: Hard cap for one question; a longer answer is cut off.

name.title: Name
name.description: What he is called: his name in the prompt, the consent line and the hint words. Renaming offers to change it in his persona too.

persona.title: Persona file
persona.description: Persona file, relative to the data directory.

language.title: Reply language
language.description: The language he always answers in, whatever language he is spoken to in. Match it to the voice: Chatterbox-Turbo speaks only English.

room.title: Room
room.description: The room the page is set to; its conversation is shared with the room's box. None: the household's.

path.title: Path
path.description: Keys from the config root, e.g. ["tts", "voice"]

value.title: Value
value.description: Any JSON value; null removes the key, so the default applies

state.title: State
state.description: waiting, ok, error, declined or expired

host.title: Host
host.description: Address winstond listens on. 127.0.0.1 keeps the API and web UI on this machine; it has no login.

port.title: Port
port.description: Port for the API and the web UI.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Talk to him in Discord DMs and get announcements there.

token_env.title: Token variable
token_env.description: The variable in data/.env that holds the Discord bot token.

allowed_user.title: Your Discord user id
allowed_user.description: The one Discord user he answers and calls "me". In Discord: Settings, Advanced, Developer Mode on, then right-click yourself, Copy User ID. Empty reads the variable under Advanced.

allowed_user_env.title: User id variable
allowed_user_env.description: The variable in data/.env read for your user id while the field above is empty; older configs kept it there.

session_idle_mins.title: Conversation resets after (min)
session_idle_mins.description: Idle minutes before a DM conversation starts fresh (and re-reads memory).

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.description: People he may message, by the name you say and their Discord user. The bot can only reach people who share a server with it.

driver.title: Driver
driver.description: How the engine is run. Docker container: Winston runs an image. Process: Winston runs a command on this machine. External server: something you run yourself; Winston only checks it.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Start it with winston up. Off keeps the entry without running it.

port.title: Port
port.description: Local port the engine listens on.

health.title: Health path
health.description: HTTP path that returns 200 when ready. Empty: no check, the engine counts as up whenever its process is (hosted APIs).

startup_timeout.title: Startup timeout (s)
startup_timeout.description: Seconds to wait for health before giving up.

args.title: Arguments
args.description: Command arguments (docker driver). {model} expands to the brain's model, {section.field} (say {tts.streaming.chunk_secs}) to that config value.

env.title: Environment
env.description: Environment variables for the engine's process or container.

volumes.title: Volumes
volumes.description: Folders the container sees: a path on this machine and where it appears inside the container.

ipc_host.title: IPC host
ipc_host.description: Share the host's IPC namespace; vLLM needs it for shared memory between workers.

url.title: URL
url.description: Base URL of an engine you run yourself (external driver).

EngineConfig.title: EngineConfig
EngineConfig.description: A heavy process Winston depends on: LLM server, TTS server, later STT. Managed by the supervisor.

name.title: Name
name.description: What you call it. Saved to Home Assistant as an alias; Home Assistant's own name is never changed.

aliases.title: Aliases
aliases.description: Other names people say for it, saved to Home Assistant as aliases.

say_first.title: Said first
say_first.description: What he says as soon as a spoken request names it (by name or alias), in place of "One moment.", before he acts. For a script that sets a scene: "Movie night it is."

quiet_after.title: Quiet after
quiet_after.description: Once a spoken request that names it has worked, he says nothing more and the box does not listen on: for a scene with music that speaks for itself. A failure is still reported.

shortcut.title: Run when named
shortcut.description: For a script: saying just one of its names ("Winston, movie night") runs it straight away without asking the model, so it does the same every time, even twice in a row. Anything longer goes to the model as usual.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Run it. Off until switched on; its card shows what it may reach first.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Its own settings, drawn from what it describes.

kinds.title: Speaking up
kinds.description: Your choices for each kind of nudge, by kind.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: Your choices for each tool, by the tool's own name. For an MCP server, only the tools listed here are offered.

memory_mb.title: Memory limit (MB)
memory_mb.description: Past this much memory it is stopped, with the reason on its card.

mcp.title: MCP server
mcp.description: Set for an MCP server added as a tools-only extension.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Let him speak up with this kind at all.

deliver.title: Deliver
deliver.description: When it is said, over the extension's own choice; one per level if you like.

where.title: Where
where.description: Where it is said, over the extension's own choice.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Offer the tool to the brain.

tier.title: Tier
tier.description: Your tier for it, over what the extension says: read runs, act runs and is logged as an action, restricted waits for you to confirm it outside the voice.

offer.title: Offer to other apps
offer.description: List it at winstond's /mcp, for Claude Code and other MCP clients.

state.title: State
state.description: stopped, starting, running, restarting, failed; or problem when it cannot run

secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.description: Its key fields and the variable each names

needs.title: Needs
needs.description: Variables it names that are not set in data/.env

nudges.title: Nudges
nudges.description: Its nudges now and those ended lately

exits.title: Exits
exits.description: Why it stopped lately, newest last

until.title: Until
until.description: Its last day; null clears it. Left out, the fact keeps its until unless the new text has a date still to come

action.title: Action
action.description: later, dismiss, mute, why, or one of the extension's actions

channel.title: Channel
channel.description: The conversation it comes from; a restricted action from one waits for your confirmation

HAApply.title: HAApply
HAApply.description: What a save (or winston ha expose) did in Home Assistant.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Connect Winston to Home Assistant: its devices as tools, sensors, units and announcement events. Off keeps the settings without using them.

url.title: URL
url.description: Home Assistant base URL on the LAN.

token_env.title: Token variable
token_env.description: The variable in data/.env that holds the long-lived access token.

mcp_path.title: MCP path
mcp_path.description: Path of Home Assistant's MCP server integration.

expose.title: Entities
expose.description: Entities he may see and control, with the names people say for them. Nothing else in Home Assistant is visible to him. Saving applies the list to Home Assistant: exposes it, un-exposes the rest and adds the aliases.

expose_domains.title: Domains
expose_domains.description: Whole domains to expose, without aliases.

verify.title: After an action
verify.description: Home Assistant says done before a device has acted. He answers straight away, then checks and corrects himself if it did not happen.

repeat.title: Repeat
repeat.description: Seconds after which a checked nudge is said again

triggers.title: Triggers
triggers.description: When its check runs, in words

muted_until.title: Muted Until
muted_until.description: Muted: 0 until switched back on, else when it ends

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Protocol the brain is spoken to with. Every supported server speaks the OpenAI chat API.

base_url.title: Base URL
base_url.description: Where the brain's OpenAI-compatible API answers, ending in /v1. Presets set it.

api_key_env.title: Key variable
api_key_env.description: The variable in data/.env that holds the API key. Unset for local servers.

model.title: Model
model.description: Model name as the server knows it. Downloaded lists what the engine can load from this machine; any other model is downloaded when the brain restarts, and the brain is offline until the download ends.

sampling.description: How the brain picks its words. The defaults suit tool calls; change them only to fix a specific habit.

thinking.description: Whether the brain reasons before it answers, per kind of channel. Better answers to hard requests, at the cost of time.

LiveEvent.title: LiveEvent
LiveEvent.description:
One thing that happened. Which fields are set depends on `type`:
state: state. user: text. reply: reply, text (a piece). reply_end: reply.
tool: call, name, status, label, ms. announcement: text. error: text.
mic: room, held_by (who has the room's mic; absent when nobody has it, core/rooms.py).
confirm: call (the confirmation's id), name (the tool), label (what it would do), status (waiting, then
ok, error, declined or expired), text (the outcome): a restricted tool waiting for you to confirm it.
nudge: call (the nudge's id), label (extension and kind), text (its plain line), name (where it went:
speakers, phone, discord, conversation, silent), links (title and url, if it has any): he spoke up,
or would have.

turns.title: Turns
turns.description: Each spoken turn kept with its audio, to find his mistakes and test changes.

tool_calls.title: Tool calls
tool_calls.description: Every tool call with its arguments and result, one JSON line each, relative to the data directory.

latency.title: Latency
latency.description: Per-turn timings (speech end, first token, first audio), one JSON line each.

command.title: Command
command.description: How to start it, for a server that talks over stdio.

url.title: Url
url.description: Where it listens, for a server that talks over HTTP.

env.title: Env
env.description: Variables from data/.env it gets; no others.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Load remembered facts into every new conversation and offer the remember tool.

dir.title: Directory
dir.description: Where the fact files live, relative to the data directory.

commit_on_write.title: Commit on write
commit_on_write.description: Commit every remembered fact to the vault's git repository, so changes can be reviewed and undone.

secs.title: Secs
secs.description: How long from now; 0 lets go.

index.title: Index
index.description: Position among the topic's facts; the end when unset

noted.title: Noted
noted.description: When it was first noted, for Undo; today when unset

until.title: Until
until.description: Its last day, for Undo; from a date still to come in the fact when unset

description.title: Description
description.description: What belongs here; a plain default when unset

state.title: State
state.description: waiting, held, said, dismissed or ended

why.title: Why
why.description: Why it waits or is held

via.title: Via
via.description: Where it was said: speakers, phone, discord, conversation, silent

put_off.title: Put Off
put_off.description: Put off until, as he was told

home_assistant.title: Home Assistant
home_assistant.description: The Home Assistant he sees and controls. Unset: no smart home.

temperature.title: Temperature
temperature.description: Degrees he speaks in. Auto follows Home Assistant's unit system.

distance.title: Units
distance.description: Kilometres, kilograms and litres, or miles, pounds and gallons.

time_format.title: Clock
time_format.description: How he says the time. Auto follows the country set in Home Assistant.

date_format.title: Dates
date_format.description: Day or month first. Auto follows the country set in Home Assistant.

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: Currency for prices, like SEK or EUR. Empty follows Home Assistant.

box.title: Box
box.description: A satellite box is set up for this room.

area.title: Area
area.description: The Home Assistant area "the lights" means here.

held_by.title: Held By
held_by.description: Who has the room's mic now; None: nobody.

screens.title: Screens
screens.description: Browser voice sessions in the room now (they follow its mic).

model.title: Model
model.description: Speech-to-text model. Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 is multilingual; v2 is English only.

quantization.title: Quantization
quantization.description: Weight precision. int8 is faster on the CPU at no audible accuracy cost; empty for full precision.

hint_words.title: Hint words
hint_words.description: Names and words he should hear right. His name, cloned voices, Discord contacts and names from the Home Assistant list are added by themselves; add the rest here, one word each, such as room names in another language.

fix_misspellings.title: Fix close misspellings
fix_misspellings.description: After speech to text, a word that sounds like a hint word and is spelled close to it becomes that word, so a misheard name comes out right. Common English words are never changed, and every change is logged as before and after.

temperature.title: Temperature
temperature.description: Lower is more reliable at tool calls.

top_p.title: Top-p
top_p.description: Samples only from the most likely tokens that add up to this share. Lower is more focused.

presence_penalty.title: Presence penalty
presence_penalty.description: Positive values push the model away from repeating itself. Qwen's chat default is 1.5; 0 calls tools more reliably.

max_tokens.title: Max tokens
max_tokens.description: Longest reply in tokens. Spoken replies are short; this is a safety cap.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Talk to him through room satellites such as Home Assistant's Voice Preview Edition. The box must not also be in Home Assistant's voice pipeline: only one client can have its microphone.

devices.title: Devices
devices.description: Satellites by room or name, e.g. "living room".

http_port.title: Audio port
http_port.description: Port the boxes fetch his spoken replies from, on every interface.

public_host.title: Address the boxes use
public_host.description: This machine's address as the boxes reach it. Unset finds it from the route to each box.

end_silence_secs.title: End of speech (s)
end_silence_secs.description: Silence after speech that ends a request.

follow_up_secs.title: Listen after a reply (s)
follow_up_secs.description: After every reply the box listens this long for more, without the wake word (at least 8 s after a question). 0: only after a question.

session_idle_mins.title: Conversation resets after (min)
session_idle_mins.description: Idle minutes before a room's conversation starts fresh: its box and the browser sessions set to that room share one.

host.title: Host
host.description: Address of the box on the LAN, an IP or its .local name.

key_env.title: Key variable
key_env.description: The variable in data/.env that holds the box's API encryption key (the one Home Assistant shows for it). Unset for a box without encryption.

wake_word.title: Wake word
wake_word.description: On-device wake word to switch on, by id (okay_nabu, hey_jarvis, hey_mycroft on a stock Voice PE; okay_winston with Winston's firmware). Several, comma separated, if the box runs more than one at a time. Unset keeps the box's choice. A long press on the box's button switches it off and on again (button only).

wake_sensitivity.title: Wake word sensitivity
wake_sensitivity.description: How readily the box wakes. More sensitive misses less and wakes by mistake more. On a stock Voice PE it covers its own wake words; Okay Winston needs Winston's firmware from 2026-09-27 on (0.95, 0.85, 0.70). Empty keeps the box's setting.

area.title: Home Assistant area
area.description: The area this room is in Home Assistant, so "turn off the lights" said here means its lights. Unset uses the room's name. Browser sessions set to the same room use it too.

level.title: Value sensor
level.description: Entity id of the value sensor.

phrases.title: Phrases
phrases.description: What you say to run it. Saying just one of these, his name and the fillers around it aside ("Okay Winston, party time"), runs the tool straight away without the model, the same every time.

tool.title: Tool
tool.description: The tool it runs: an extension tool as "extension.tool" ("spotify.party"), or a Home Assistant script as "script.name". The tool must be available to the brain.

args.title: Arguments
args.description: Fixed arguments passed to the tool every time, e.g. which track a party plays and which light scene it runs.

say_first.title: Said first
say_first.description: What he says the instant you say it, before it runs, in place of "One moment.". For a party: "Here we go, sir."

quiet_after.title: Quiet after
quiet_after.description: Once it has worked he says nothing more and the box does not listen on: for a scene with music that speaks for itself. A failure is still reported.

voice.title: Voice
voice.description: Speak in this voice instead of tts.voice (a clip name under the server's voices directory, or a voice the server knows)

streaming.description: Try these streaming settings instead of the saved ones. Reaches the speech server only when its engine command uses {tts.streaming.*}; otherwise ignored (X-Streaming).

enabled.title: Stream speech
enabled.description: Start speaking before a sentence is fully rendered: first audio in about 0.3 s instead of up to 2 s for a long sentence, with a join between chunks that can sound a little choppy. Off renders whole sentences. For the Chatterbox server.

chunk_secs.title: Chunk length (s)
chunk_secs.description: Audio per chunk after the first. Longer means fewer joins and smoother speech; how soon he starts talking depends only on the first chunk.

first_secs.title: First chunk (s)
first_secs.description: Audio rendered before anything is sent. Shorter starts sooner; below about 0.9 s the second chunk can arrive late and leave a short gap.

lookahead_secs.title: Look-ahead (s)
lookahead_secs.description: Audio held back at the end of each chunk until the sounds after it are known. More smooths the joins but makes the first chunk shorter.

SpeakStreaming.title: SpeakStreaming
SpeakStreaming.description: tts.streaming for this request only; unset fields keep the saved values.

home.title: You
home.description: The person entity that says whether you are home: for nudges held until you get home, spoken at home and sent to your phone away, and extensions allowed to know.

phone.title: Your phone
phone.description: The Home Assistant notify service that reaches your phone (the companion app's): nudges while you are away, and confirming restricted calls. Empty: Discord, when it is set up.
phone.placeholder: None: Discord, when it is set up

max_per_day.title: Spoken nudges a day
max_per_day.description: Past this many spoken nudges in a day, the rest wait for the next morning's briefing. What you asked for (reminders, a time you gave) does not count.

briefing_from.title: Briefing from
briefing_from.description: The morning briefing is given at your first conversation after this time, or when you ask what's new.

fallback_time.title: After work
fallback_time.description: "Remind me after work" when he does not know when you finish: when you get home that day, or at this time if you are home already.

day_parts.title: Parts of the day
day_parts.description: What "tomorrow morning" and "this evening" mean when you put something off.

origin.title: Origin
origin.description: The session handing over messages; its own come back to it never.

epoch.title: Epoch
epoch.description: The room conversation the session last saw; None at its start.

after.title: After
after.description: How many of the room's messages the session has taken in.

messages.title: Messages
messages.description: The session's new messages, OpenAI chat format.

pull.title: Pull
pull.description: False: only hand over (after a reply); nothing comes back.

seq.title: Seq
seq.description: The room's message count after this call.

reset.title: Reset
reset.description: The session's epoch is not the room's: its context is from an older conversation, and `others` is the whole of this one.

seqs.title: Seqs
seqs.description: Each of `others`' place in the room's messages.

base_url.title: Base URL
base_url.description: Where the speech server's OpenAI speech API answers, ending in /v1. Presets set it.

api_key_env.title: Key variable
api_key_env.description: The variable in data/.env that holds the API key. Unset for local servers.

voice.title: Voice
voice.description: Voice name sent to the server. OpenAI names map to the server's default clip.

sample_rate.title: Sample rate
sample_rate.description: Audio rate the speech server returns, in Hz.

streaming.title: Streaming
streaming.description: How speech is cut into chunks so he starts talking before a sentence is fully rendered.

enabled.title: Stream speech
enabled.description: Start speaking before a sentence is fully rendered: first audio in about 0.3 s instead of up to 2 s for a long sentence, with a join between chunks that can sound a little choppy. Off renders whole sentences. For the Chatterbox server.

chunk_secs.title: Chunk length (s)
chunk_secs.description: Audio per chunk after the first. Longer means fewer joins and smoother speech; how soon he starts talking depends only on the first chunk.

first_secs.title: First chunk (s)
first_secs.description: Audio rendered before anything is sent. Shorter starts sooner; below about 0.9 s the second chunk can arrive late and leave a short gap.

lookahead_secs.title: Look-ahead (s)
lookahead_secs.description: Audio held back at the end of each chunk until the sounds after it are known. More smooths the joins but makes the first chunk shorter.

TTSStreamingConfig.title: TTSStreamingConfig
TTSStreamingConfig.description:
Reaches the speech server through `{tts.streaming.*}` in its engine command; the Chatterbox preset
passes them. Pocket TTS streams on its own and has no such arguments.

voice.title: Voice
voice.description: Reasoning before answering on the voice channel. Costs seconds.

text.title: Text
text.description: Reasoning on text channels. Much better at multi-part requests.

home.title: Home requests
home.description: Reasoning on a spoken request about the home (a light, a lamp, the PC), even with voice off. About 1 s slower at medium effort; without it he sometimes said a light was on without switching it.

home_effort.title: Home request effort
home_effort.description: How long he reasons about a home request, for chat templates that take a reasoning effort (Qwen3.8: low, medium, xhigh; gpt-oss: low, medium, high). Medium was as right as xhigh on the 27B and about twice as fast. Empty uses the template's default.

control.title: Control
control.description: How the server is told to think or not: chat_template for vLLM and llama.cpp (enable_thinking), reasoning_effort for Ollama, none for servers without a switch.

waiting.title: Waiting
waiting.description: A restricted tool waiting for your confirmation

sensors.title: Sensors
sensors.description: Watched sensors by label; readings come with their age.

web_search.title: Web search
web_search.description: A cloud search for current facts: news, opening hours, prices.

ask_claude.title: Ask Claude
ask_claude.description: Claude in the cloud for questions too hard for the local brain.

description.title: Description
description.description: What belongs here; kept when unset, removed when empty

enabled.title: Keep turns
enabled.description: Keep each spoken turn: the audio of what you said, what he heard, what he did and said, and how long each step took. Used to find and mark his mistakes and to test changes on them. Stays on this machine.

keep_days.title: Keep for (days)
keep_days.description: Days a turn is kept; older days are removed.

dir.title: Folder
dir.description: Where turns are kept, relative to the data directory.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Voice activity detector that decides when you are speaking.

stop_secs.title: End of speech (s)
stop_secs.description: Silence after speech before the utterance is sent.

unfinished_stop_secs.title: Pause when unfinished (s)
unfinished_stop_secs.description: Extra wait after silence when the turn detector thinks the sentence is unfinished. One-word answers pay this in full.

enabled.title: Check after an action
enabled.description: After he turns something on or off or sets a light, he reads its state from Home Assistant and says so when it did not change ("The shelf lamp did not respond."). His answer is not delayed; the correction follows it.

wait_secs.title: Give up after (s)
wait_secs.description: Seconds a device has to show the change before he says it did not. He reads it at 0.5 s, 1.5 s and this, and stops as soon as it matches.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Talk to him by voice from the browser. Room satellites have their own channel.

host.title: Host
host.description: Address the voice channel listens on. 127.0.0.1 keeps it on this machine; winstond passes the browser's offer to it.

port.title: Port
port.description: Port the voice channel listens on; Pipecat's own test page is served here too.

session_idle_mins.title: Conversation resets after (min)
session_idle_mins.description: Idle minutes before the Talk page's typed conversation starts fresh (and re-reads memory).

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Let him look up current facts on the web. Only the search question leaves the house.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Search backend. gemini: Gemini with Google Search grounding (needs billing enabled on the key).

model.title: Model
model.description: Flash-Lite answers in about 1.4 s, Flash in 2.3 s (minimal thinking, measured 2026-09-23).

thinking.title: Thinking
thinking.description: Reasoning at the search model. Each step up costs about a second.

api_key_env.title: Key variable
api_key_env.description: The variable in data/.env that holds the Gemini API key.

max_per_day.title: Searches per day
max_per_day.description: Hard cap; past it the tool refuses until midnight.

timeout.title: Timeout (s)
timeout.description: Seconds before a search gives up and he says it could not look it up.

version.title: Version
version.description: Config file format version. Winston sets it.

engines.title: Engines
engines.description: Heavy processes Winston runs or checks, by name: llm for the brain's server, tts for the speech server.

extensions.title: Extensions
extensions.description: Each extension by its id: whether it runs, its settings, and your choices for its tools and nudges.

shortcuts.title: Shortcuts
shortcuts.description: Spoken phrases that run a tool straight away, without the model: a scene, a party. Each names a tool and the fixed arguments it runs with.
